hardware: Intel Core i7-12700H, 16 GB RAM, NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop 6 GB, HP performance mode, plugged in

proposals.statement: The client's current system has a paper diary that receptionists use to manage bookings, which leads to missed calls and double bookings

evidence.quote: All three clinics, Centurion, Irene and Olievenhoutbosch, have their own landline and their own paper diary at reception. The receptionist finds a gap, writes the pet's name and the owner's number in pencil, and that's it.

Mornings are the worst. Between eight and ten the phones just don't stop, and there's one receptionist per clinic who is also checking people in and taking payments. We miss a lot of calls. And people get double-booked, because someone rubbed out a booking and someone else wrote over it.

proposals.statement: The client wants to reduce missed calls, double bookings, and no-shows by implementing an online booking system

evidence.quote: The goals are fewer missed calls, no double bookings, and fewer no-shows?
If I had to pick one, it's the phones. My receptionists are burning out.

proposals.statement: The client currently uses VetDesk Pro for clinical records, owners' details, vaccination history, and billing, but it does not have a proper diary

evidence.quote: VetDesk Pro, yes. That's where all the clinical records live, the owners' details, vaccination history, billing. But it has no proper diary.

proposals.statement: The client experiences high call volume in the morning that causes missed calls and double bookings due to the paper diary system

evidence.quote: Mornings are the worst. Between eight and ten the phones just don't stop, and there's one receptionist per clinic who is also checking people in and taking payments. We miss a lot of calls. And people get double-booked, because someone rubbed out a booking and someone else wrote over it.

proposals.statement: The client has approximately twenty no-shows per week across all three clinics, each representing a thirty-minute slot that goes unused

evidence.quote: We have maybe twenty no-shows a week across the three clinics. Each one is a thirty-minute slot gone.

proposals.statement: The client wants to allow pet owners to book appointments online through a website on their phone

evidence.quote: They go onto a website on their phone, pick the clinic, pick what it's for, a vaccination, a check-up, a sick pet, and see the open times. They choose one and it's booked. And then they get a reminder the day before.

proposals.statement: The client wants to send vaccination reminders automatically to owners via a link to book

evidence.quote: If that could go out automatically with a link to book, that's half the work gone.

proposals.statement: The client wants receptionists to be able to see the day's schedule for their clinic, move bookings around, and handle phone bookings

evidence.quote: They need to see the day for their clinic, move bookings around, and put in phone bookings too, because some of our older clients will never book online.

proposals.statement: The client has a high volume of appointments that doubles during vaccination season due to annual vaccinations and rabies drives

evidence.quote: Hugely. Annual vaccinations bunch up in February and March, because so many of our clients got their puppies at Christmas, and then there's the rabies drive in March as well. It easily doubles then.

proposals.statement: The online booking system must only show bookings and reminders, not medical history

evidence.quote: No. Definitely not, not in this project. The vets don't want owners reading clinical notes without someone explaining them. Bookings and reminders only.

proposals.statement: The project budget is one hundred and eighty thousand rand for development and two and a half thousand rand per month for running costs

evidence.quote: We've put aside a hundred and eighty thousand rand to build it. And the running costs, the messages and the hosting, must stay under two and a half thousand a month for all three clinics. That's my limit.

proposals.statement: The system must be live by the first of February to handle vaccination season

evidence.quote: Before vaccination season. So live by the first of February at the latest.
Ideally mid-January, so the girls have two weeks to get used to it before the rush.

proposals.statement: The website should use the client's green color scheme with large buttons and no app download

evidence.quote: Our green, the logo green. Big buttons, because half the people booking are holding a puppy in the other hand. And no app to download, just a web page.

proposals.statement: VetDesk's API requires per-clinic charges and takes three months to activate for clinics

evidence.quote: There is an API. Our rep mentioned it at a conference.
But they charge for it per clinic, and when the Pretoria East practice asked for it, it took VetDesk three months to switch it on.

proposals.statement: The system must have a simple interface with one screen to reduce complexity

evidence.quote: And simple. One screen if possible. The VetDesk screens have about forty fields on them, I don't want that.

proposals.statement: Online pet food ordering and payment are planned for next year

evidence.quote: Ordering pet food online and paying for it, maybe. Next year.
